note: THE FIXTURE BAR quince#80 set, half one: a declared-blocking issue gains a comment while the session holds a stale read of it, and an event must fire AND NAME THE ISSUE. This is the escalation channel. The measured case is the ruling on quince#44, which landed as a comment on an issue while the architect's blocked list was quince#70/#71/#72/#75/#78/#80 — most with no PR at all — and the only reason it was ever seen was 'a hand re-read I'd committed to when filing the issue'. A human-remembers mitigation at the head of the one channel that carries authority. Two events fire, not one, and that is deliberate: `issue-comment` is the typed event a blocked session acts on, and `issue-updated` is the unconditional backstop, exactly as `updated` is on the PR half. A backstop that trusts the classifier is not a backstop.
